data.long_meaning: The name Dakshith is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Dakshina’, which means ‘South’, ‘Dakshinaka’, meaning ‘Southern direction’, and ‘Dakshita’, meaning ‘Dedicated to God’. In Hindu mythology, Lord Shiva is referred to as Dakshinamurthy, who imparts wisdom and knowledge. The name Dakshith is given to a boy as a symbol of dedication to the divine and the pursuit of knowledge and wisdom.

historical_references.reference: Dakshinamurti is a form of Shiva, depicted as a teacher imparting wisdom to his disciples. This image finds its origin in the Upanishads, specifically the Shvetashvatara Upanishad, where Shiva is described as 'the one who imparts the knowledge from the southern direction'.

Dakshina means 'southern' in Sanskrit, and was the name of the land of the Cholas, a prominent dynasty in ancient Tamil Nadu, India. The name may have originated from the geographical location of the kingdom, which lies in the southern part of the Indian subcontinent.
